title: Exact phase diagram of the XXZ Heisenberg chain in a staggered magnetic field
abstract: We study the phase diagram of the spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain in a staggered magnetic field. An exact solution is obtained along the phase boundary, where the exchange anisotropy and the staggered-field strength satisfy an exact analytical relation, yielding a highly degenerate manifold of ground states with off-diagonal long-range order. We demonstrate that these exact ground states lie on the boundary between the ferromagnetic phase and a gapless Luttinger liquid phase. Upon further decreasing the anisotropy, the gapless phase eventually gives way to a gapped quantum-disordered phase. Large-scale density-matrix renormalization group calculations confirm this phase structure and indicate that the transition across the exact boundary is of first order. Our results provide an exact benchmark for understanding quantum phase transitions driven by staggered magnetic fields in one-dimensional quantum spin systems.
summary: This work maps the quantum phase diagram of the XXZ Heisenberg chain under a staggered magnetic field, finding an exact solution along the boundary $\Delta = \cosh q$. This boundary separates a ferromagnetic phase from a gapless Luttinger liquid, and the transition across this line is shown to be first order. The combination of exact algebra and DMRG provides a rigorous benchmark for understanding quantum criticality in 1D magnets.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the exact phase diagram of the spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain when subjected to a staggered magnetic field.
main_result: The paper establishes an exact phase boundary ($\Delta = \cosh q$) where the ground state exhibits Off-Diagonal Long-Range Order, separating a ferromagnetic phase from a gapless Luttinger liquid phase.
method: The research combines finding an exact solution along a specific resonant phase boundary with large-scale Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations for confirmation.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain on a ring, described by a Hamiltonian incorporating exchange anisotropy ($\Delta$) and a staggered magnetic field ($h = \sinh q$).
key_observables: Off-diagonal long-range order (ODLRO), energy gap ($E_{	ext{gap}}$), correlation length ($\xi$), and staggered magnetization ($m_{	ext{stag}}$).
important_parameters: The anisotropy ($\Delta$) and the staggered field parameter ($q$), with the critical resonant condition being $\Delta = \cosh q$.
main_assumptions: The exact solvability is restricted to the resonant condition $\Delta = \cosh q$, and the perturbative analysis has limitations as system size increases.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the phase diagram in the $(q, \Delta)$ plane, mapping ferromagnetic, gapless Luttinger liquid, and gapped quantum-disordered regions. Figures 2 and 3 use DMRG to track gap and magnetization across these regions.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the Hamiltonian and the physical problem. It then derives the exact solution along the resonant boundary ($\Delta = \cosh q$), demonstrating the highly degenerate ground state manifold. Finally, it uses DMRG to map out the full phase diagram and characterize the nature of the transitions.
why_interesting: The finding of an exactly solvable, highly degenerate ground state manifold driven by a staggered field provides an exact benchmark for understanding quantum phase transitions in 1D quantum spin systems, which is crucial for modeling correlated materials.
